(clopidogrel) Pharmacopoeias. In US. USP 31 (Clopidogrel Bisulfate). A white to off-white powder. Freely soluble in water and in methyl alcohol; practically insolu- ble in ether. Adverse Effects and Precautions As for Ticlopidine, p.1411. The incidence of adverse effects, particularly blood dyscrasias, is lower with clopidogrel, although fatali- ties have been reported (see Effects on the Blood, p.1411). Routine blood counts are not necessary, although they should be performed promptly when clinical signs suggest blood dyscrasias.
